profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page, this building, VA2, is located at 12098 Sunrise Valley Drive, Reston, VA 20191, part of CoreSite's three-building Reston campus alongside VA1 and VA3. CoreSite publishes 192,000-plus square feet for this building; no MW capacity or opening year is stated, and the operator's spec-sheet landing page for VA2 adds no further quantitative detail beyond the main page. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance for its facilities generally.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to this Reston campus. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates raising a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class for data centers effective January 1, 2027, under which facilities with 25 megawatts or more of demand face 14-year mandatory contracts and minimum cost-coverage requirements, per Inside Climate News. Reston sits within the broader Northern Virginia "Data Center Alley" corridor anchored by Loudoun County, though closer to the DC Beltway than the larger wholesale campuses tracked elsewhere in this registry.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance; the company also budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026. As the smallest of the three Reston buildings by CoreSite's own published square footage, VA2 rounds out a campus whose interconnection density has made Reston a secondary hub distinct from the larger wholesale campuses further out in Loudoun County.

reading.body:
CoreSite VA2 Reston occupies 192,000 square feet as part of a three-building campus in Fairfax County, Virginia. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity or power specification for this building. Without a published figure, the scale of IT load that VA2 can support remains unknown from available operator data.

Virginia's regulatory environment now directly constrains data center expansion. In November 2026, regulators approved new Dominion Energy rates effective January 2027 that impose 14-year mandatory contracts and cost-coverage minimums on any facility drawing 25 megawatts or more. This rate class restructuring affects the economics of all Northern Virginia campuses, including VA2. The facility holds SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA certifications, qualifying it for regulated workloads and government computing.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite sites in mid-2026 and raised its full-year guidance on that strength, budgeting $695 million in data center development spending. VA2 ranks as the published-capacity-wise smaller of its three-building Reston campus, which sits in Northern Virginia's secondary interconnection corridor closer to DC than to the larger wholesale campuses tracked in Loudoun County. Without a published power figure, VA2's contribution to that momentum cannot be quantified from operator disclosures alone.
